bug_semantics: Attacker-controlled ProcessingInstruction data containing the XML closing delimiter ?> is retained without validation and was serialized verbatim between <?target and ?>. The embedded delimiter terminates the processing instruction early, so following attacker text is parsed as live XML nodes when the serialized document is consumed.
flaw_origin: The direct parent already allowed arbitrary data to be stored on a ProcessingInstruction, but it had no XMLSerializer or serializeToString sink. Commit 5fb8fb92b2cb9d7c6b8b5477900e90619b14e432 introduced that sink and its PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION_NODE branch, concatenating node.data directly before ?> with no delimiter check; this is the first public Git object that completes the vulnerable source-to-sink path.
ai_marker: absent — the BIC commit object has author and committer jindw <jindw@xidea.org>, an empty commit message/body, no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, and no bot identity
evidence: CVE.org API record CVE-2026-41675 is PUBLISHED and describes XML node injection through unvalidated PI data; it marks xmldom <=0.6.0, @xmldom/xmldom <0.8.13, and @xmldom/xmldom >=0.9.0,<0.9.10 affected.
GitHub advisory API GHSA-x6wf-f3px-wcqx has withdrawn_at=null, names first patched versions 0.8.13 and 0.9.10, and references direct fix 7207a4b0e0bcc228868075ed991665ef9f73b1c2.

git grep on parent tree 5d770d4c04466fd4a99b0762d28b8d1d111ba0c7 finds no XMLSerializer, serializeToString, or PI-output buf.push sink anywhere; dom.js:552-557 only constructs a ProcessingInstruction and stores target/data.

git diff 5d770d4c04466fd4a99b0762d28b8d1d111ba0c7..5fb8fb92b2cb9d7c6b8b5477900e90619b14e432 shows the new serializer in dom.js:767-833, including case PROCESSING_INSTRUCTION_NODE returning buf.push('<?', node.nodeName, ' ', node.data, '?>') without checking node.data.

git show -s --format=raw 5fb8fb92b2cb9d7c6b8b5477900e90619b14e432 proves the BIC has exactly one parent, 5d770d4c04466fd4a99b0762d28b8d1d111ba0c7, author/committer jindw <jindw@xidea.org>, and no commit message or trailers; there is no commit-object AI marker.
git tag --contains 5fb8fb92b2cb9d7c6b8b5477900e90619b14e432 starts at 0.1.0, and git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms the BIC is in 0.1.0 and later vulnerable history, including legacy xmldom 0.6.0.

Direct fix 7207a4b0e0bcc228868075ed991665ef9f73b1c2 adds requireWellFormed guards in lib/dom.js:3082-3096, including rejection of PI data containing ?> before the existing serializer concatenation; its parent is fda7cc313de30243fea35cada64e0bb12099c2a1.

git tag --contains 7207a4b0e0bcc228868075ed991665ef9f73b1c2 starts at 0.9.10, and merge-base confirms it is an ancestor of tag 0.9.10; the LTS-equivalent direct fix c6874ab39b95852036ed65f0422c1893c5a01775 is an ancestor of tag 0.8.13.
The fixes are opt-in: with requireWellFormed=true they reject unsafe PI data, while the default serializer remains verbatim as documented by the advisory and both fix commit messages.
reasoning: The vulnerability requires both attacker-controlled PI data and an XML serialization sink. Although the parent stored arbitrary PI data, direct inspection of the entire parent tree found no serializer, so it did not contain the advisory's source-to-sink mechanism. The single-parent BIC introduced XML serialization and the exact unsafe PI concatenation in one public commit; no move, prior sink, merge member, or finer public commit exists to decompose. Its immediate parent therefore directly verifies absence. The BIC predates every affected release line, beginning before 0.1.0, while the main direct guard is contained in 0.9.10 and its LTS counterpart is contained in 0.8.13, matching the advisory and published CVE boundaries. The BIC commit object has human author/committer identities and no AI marker, so the real vulnerability is NOT_AI regardless of any AI signal elsewhere in repository history.
